subject: Global variables for a session in R.

messages.author: d6f9c6ff776783d5
messages.subject: Global variables for a session in R.
parts:
Hi,

I saw the scoping part to work with local, and global variables, but there does not work, and I do not why.

My problem is that I create a local variable, and I want to modified in a reactive function, but does not change, a specific example is something like this:

shinyServer(function(input, output){ 
    localV1 <- "something"
    
    function1 <- reactive({
        localV1<-"something more"
    })
    
    function2<-reactive({
        return(localV1)
    }) 
})

so, I have a variable localV1 with a text, and I change this text in a function1(), but when I call the function2() the text of localV1 is "something" and does not "something more"


Thanks for all!

messages.author: a814dd0eade31e3e
messages.subject: Re: Global variables for a session in R.
parts:
Try using <<- instead of <-

Your example is stylized so I am not sure how function1 will be used. You may need to use return(function1()) in function2. This part of the Shiny tutorial might be useful: http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity-overview

Also, consider using a reactive value

values <- reactiveValues()
values$localV1 <- "something"

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Global variables for a session in R.
parts:
Vincent is right - you'll probably want to restructure your code. The reason why is because function2 will never be invalidated (after the first time). That means that when localV1 changes, it won't trigger function2 to re-execute and send a new value to something that uses function2().

-Winston
